construction_markdown:
### Audited conversion, not a new leaderboard construction

Let `D=2^d` and let `A_s:F_2^K→F_2^m`, `s∈[D]`, be deterministic binary-linear maps. Define

`c_x(s,u)=<u,A_sx>`, for `(s,u)∈[D]×F_2^m`.

If `z(x)=|{s:A_sx=0}|`, then

`wt(c_x)=2^(m-1)(D-z(x))`.

Thus `d+m=30` and `z(x)≤D/512` for every nonzero `x` give an injective binary-linear `[2^30,K,≥535822336]` code.

The affine version takes `B_sx=(b_0,b')∈F_2×F_2^m` and outputs `b_0+<u,b'>`. If `z_i(x)=|{s:B_sx=i e_0}|`, its normalized signed sum is exactly `(z_0(x)-z_1(x))/D`; hence the exact one-sided requirement is `z_0(x)-z_1(x)≤D/512`.

No family audited here supplies these conditions with `K≥1041`.

Consequently `d+m=30` and `z(x)≤D/512` for all nonzero `x` give the immutable distance exactly. A strong entropy-one lossless condenser of error at most `2^-10` implies this kernel bound.

distance_audit: For a binary word of length `N`, normalized signed sum is `β=1-2 wt/N`; the required distance is equivalent to the one-sided condition `β≤1/512`.
In the homogeneous character conversion, every killed seed contributes an all-zero block and every other seed contributes a balanced block, proving `β=z(x)/D` for every nonzero message.
In the affine conversion, the symbols `0` and `e_0` contribute signed sums `+2^m` and `-2^m`; all other symbols contribute zero. Hence `β=(z_0-z_1)/D` exactly.
The condition `z(x)≤D/512<D` also proves injectivity, so the dimension is exactly the input dimension whenever a qualifying family is supplied.
No new code is claimed, so no minimum-distance value is reported as a leaderboard parameter.
explicitness_audit: All audited conversions use the complete lexicographically ordered coordinate set `[D]×F_2^m`; there is no sampling, padding, or hidden shortening.
The polynomial-family ceilings quantify over every integer field degree, seed-set size, and polynomial dimension satisfying exact length.
The bad polynomial used to prove necessity has prescribed evaluation roots; its scale is the least field element outside an explicitly defined forbidden set.
The GUV and Ta-Shma conclusions use their displayed finite formulas, not hidden asymptotic constants.
The shared lemma-book and roadmap directories were empty at the final audit; every then-present message-board and durable-submission file was read.
Because this is an obstruction rather than a publication candidate and the workspace is read-only, no proof file or record was written and no publication validator/build was run.

obstructions: A standard extractor is not the correct primitive: individual kernel control follows from entropy-one lossless condensation, not from extraction at a higher entropy threshold.
For `K>m`, a strong linear extractor from min-entropy `m` to all `m` output bits has error at least `(2^m-1)/(2(2^(m+1)-1))≥1/6`, far above `2^-10`.
The 2-universal/leftover-hash certificate gives `K≤30` under homogeneous character descent and `K≤31` under affine descent.
The exact AGHP polynomial-powering family has maximum dimension 975.
Univariate polynomial hashing with affine Hadamard descent has the unique finite maximum 1040 at field degree 16, 32,768 seeds, and 65 field coefficients.
Direct GUV lossless condensation needs at least 33 seed bits before output-character enumeration.
Ta-Shma's published fallback needs at least 64 walk steps here and therefore has support greater than `2^30` at rank 1041; its near-optimal branch's finite prerequisite fails.
The hypothetical `[32768,17,16383]_2` inner code is impossible; the resulting dimension-17 field-linear product route is capped at 1037.
These are scoped family and certificate obstructions, not an upper bound for arbitrary extractor-based or binary-linear constructions.

proof_markdown:
## Scope

The claim is a finite obstruction for standard extractor-to-code routes, not an impossibility theorem for all extractors.

## 1. Character conversion

For fixed nonzero `x`, if `A_sx=0`, the block indexed by `s` is all zero. Otherwise `u↦<u,A_sx>` is a nonzero linear functional and is balanced. Therefore

`wt(c_x)=2^(m-1)(D-z(x))`

and its normalized signed sum is `z(x)/D`. Since the total length is `D2^m`, the target is met exactly when `z(x)≤D/512`. This also makes the encoder injective.

For affine maps `B_sx=(b_0,b')`, the inner block is all zero at symbol `0`, all one at symbol `e_0`, and balanced otherwise. Hence its signed sum is exactly `(z_0-z_1)/D`, establishing the two-fiber criterion.

## 2. Lossless condensers imply the kernel condition

Let `X` be uniform on `{0,x}` and let `S` be uniform on `[D]`. For every seed killing `x`, the distribution of `(S,A_SX)` has an atom of mass `1/D`. Any distribution of min-entropy at least `d+1` has every atom of mass at most `1/(2D)`. Thus these atoms contribute at least `z(x)/(2D)` to total variation. A strong entropy-one lossless condenser of error `η` consequently satisfies `z(x)/D≤2η`. Taking `η≤2^-10` proves the required bound.

## 3. Ordinary extraction and universal hashing

For completeness, suppose a strong linear extractor maps `F_2^K` to `F_2^m` and must extract from every `m`-dimensional flat. For a uniformly random `m`-subspace `V`, a fixed full-rank seed map is injective on `V` with probability at most `2^m/(2^(m+1)-1)`; on every other `V`, its output is supported on a subspace of size at most `2^(m-1)` and is at total variation at least `1/2` from uniform. Averaging over `V` and seeds gives error at least `(2^m-1)/(2(2^(m+1)-1))≥1/6`.

For a 2-universal family with alphabet size `q`, the outer words have distance at least `(1-1/q)D`. If their number is `M`, shorten on a most frequent symbol in one coordinate and apply the strict q-ary Plotkin bound to the resulting length-`D-1` code; this gives `M≤qD`. Therefore exact homogeneous length `qD=2^30` gives `K≤30`, while affine-Hadamard length `qD/2=2^30` gives `K≤31`.

## 4. Exact AGHP ceiling

Take `F=F_(2^m)`, an explicit subset `X⊂F` of size `2^a`, and messages `P∈F[T]` of degree below `t`. Enumerate `(x,y)∈X×F` and output `Tr(yP(x))`. For nonzero `P`, averaging over `y` shows that the signed bias is exactly `|{x∈X:P(x)=0}|/2^a`. Thus the family is injective for `t≤2^a`, has dimension `mt`, and meets the target exactly when `t-1≤2^(a-9)`; if this inequality fails, a product of `t-1` distinct linear factors from `X` is a violating word.

Exact length gives `a+m=30`, while `X⊂F` gives `a≤m`. Maximizing yields

`mt≤(30-a)(2^(a-9)+1)≤975`,

with the unique maximum `a=m=15`, `t=65`.

## 5. Exact affine polynomial-hashing ceiling

Let `q=2^r`, use `D` distinct evaluation seeds, and evaluate degree-below-`t` polynomials over `F_q`. Identify each field symbol with `RM(1,r-1)=[q/2,r,q/4]_2`. Exact length forces

`Dq/2=2^30`, so `D=2^(31-r)`.

Distinct evaluation requires `D≤q`, hence `r≥16`. The product-distance calculation requires `t-1≤D/512`. This is also necessary: if `R=t-1>D/512`, prescribe `R` evaluation roots and scale the polynomial so that all remaining values avoid the unique all-one inner symbol. Such a scale exists because `q-1>D-R`. The resulting word has weight `(D-R)q/4`, strictly below the target.

Consequently

`K=rt≤r(1+2^(22-r))`.

For `r=16,...,22` the bounds are `1040,561,306,171,100,63,44`; for `r≥23`, `t=1` and `K≤r≤31`. The unique maximum is the shared `r=16,D=32768,t=65,K=1040` construction.

## 6. Direct GUV and Ta-Shma specializations

[GUV Theorem 4.2](https://people.seas.harvard.edu/~salil/research/PVcondenser-ccc.pdf) gives

`d_seed=(1+1/α)(log n_G+log k_max+log(1/η)+α+2)`.

For `n_G≥1041`, `k_max=1`, and `η≤2^-10`, put `A=log_2(n_G)+12>22`. Then

`d_seed=A+1+α+A/α ≥ A+1+2 sqrt(A)>32.409`.

Thus the integer seed length is at least 33, already exceeding the entire 30-bit coordinate budget.

For [Ta-Shma's finite fallback](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Papers/T.STOC17.pdf), `ζ=0.82+2λ≥0.82` and `t=2 ceil(log_ζ(2^-9))≥64`. Its support `n_0D^t`, with `n_0≥1041` and nontrivial `D≥2`, is greater than `2^30`. The near-optimal branch is unavailable because for `α≤0.01`, `α^3/(2log_2(1/α))≤7.53·10^-8<1/9`.

## 7. Closest inner-code loophole

The shared residual lemma rules out `[32768,17,16383]_2`. Indeed, Griesmer equality and successive residualization would yield `[9,5,4]_2`. A parity-check matrix for that code would require nine distinct nonzero vectors in `F_2^4` with no zero-sum triple. If `S` were such a set and `x∈S`, then `S` and `x+S` would be disjoint, contradicting `2|S|≤16`.

Hence a dimension-17 inner code has distance at most 16,382. A product-distance proof needs outer distance at least 32,708, so Singleton bounds a length-32,768 outer code by dimension 61. The final dimension is at most `17·61=1037`.

All audited standard routes therefore fail to exceed 1040.

proof_steps.proof: For every binary word, `β=1-2 wt/N`. Substitution of `N=2^30` and `β≤2^-9` gives `wt≥2^29-2^20=535822336`.
proof_steps.statement: The target distance is equivalent to one-sided normalized signed bias at most `1/512`.

proof_steps.proof: Each killed seed contributes an all-zero block; every nonkilled seed gives a balanced nonzero linear functional.
proof_steps.statement: The homogeneous character conversion has `wt(c_x)=2^(m-1)(D-z(x))` and bias `z(x)/D`.

proof_steps.proof: Apply the condenser to the flat source uniform on `{0,x}`. Every killed seed creates excess atom mass at least `1/(2D)`, so total variation is at least `z(x)/(2D)`.
proof_steps.statement: A strong entropy-one lossless condenser of error `η` satisfies `z(x)/D≤2η`.

proof_steps.proof: Average over random `m`-subspaces and use the probability that a fixed rank-`m` map is injective on such a subspace.
proof_steps.statement: For `K>m`, extraction from min-entropy `m` to `m` linear output bits has error at least `(2^m-1)/(2(2^(m+1)-1))≥1/6`.

proof_steps.proof: A 2-universal family gives a q-ary code of distance `(1-1/q)D`; one-coordinate shortening followed by strict Plotkin gives at most `qD` words.
proof_steps.statement: Universal hashing yields `K≤30` in the homogeneous conversion and `K≤31` in the affine conversion.

proof_steps.proof: Bias is the exact evaluation-root fraction. Exact support and the root bound reduce the optimization to `(30-a)(2^(a-9)+1)`, whose maximum is 975.
proof_steps.statement: The direct AGHP polynomial-powering family has exact finite ceiling `K=975`.

proof_steps.proof: Root counting gives the sufficient bound; a prescribed-root polynomial scaled to avoid the all-one inner symbol proves necessity. Finite optimization over `16≤r≤31` gives 1040.
proof_steps.statement: Univariate polynomial hashing with affine Hadamard descent has unique maximum `K=1040`.

proof_steps.proof: Substitute `n_G≥1041`, `k_max=1`, and `η≤2^-10` into GUV Theorem 4.2 and minimize over `α` by AM–GM.
proof_steps.statement: Direct GUV condensation needs at least 33 seed bits and cannot fit exact length `2^30`.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed fallback parameters force `t≥64`, `n_0≥1041`, and `D≥2`; the near-optimal branch prerequisite also fails numerically.
proof_steps.statement: Ta-Shma's published direct schedules do not fit this finite target at rank 1041.

proof_steps.proof: Repeated residualization yields the impossible `[9,5,4]` code; Singleton then bounds the remaining product route by `17·61`.
proof_steps.statement: The dimension-17 equal-block field-linear product route is capped at 1037.

research_direction: Extractor-based linear codes: exact linear-condenser conversion and finite family ceilings
theorem_statement: The exact entropy-one linear-condenser character conversion reduces the target to a killed-seed fraction at most `1/512`. At length `2^30`, ordinary 2-universal hashing is capped at dimension 31, direct AGHP polynomial powering at 975, and univariate affine polynomial hashing at the shared optimum 1040; direct GUV and Ta-Shma finite schedules exceed the coordinate budget. Therefore none of these standard extractor families yields dimension at least 1041. This is a scoped obstruction, not a global upper bound.
title: Exact finite ceilings for standard extractor-to-code conversions
